one_sentence: The harmonic series and trinitarian theology share a generative topology of single-source derivation, perfect imaging, dynamic motion, and threefold minimal completeness.
executive_summary: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between music theory (harmonic series, consonance/dissonance, tonal gravity) and Christian trinitarian theology. The core claim is that both domains exhibit a single-source generative topology: all harmonic structure derives from one fundamental frequency, just as all divine persons derive from one Father. Key evidence includes the harmonic series generating pitch material, the octave as a perfect image of the fundamental, the fifth introducing dynamic motion, and the triad as the minimal structure for harmonic completeness—mirroring the Son as image, the Spirit as mover, and the Trinity as minimal relational completeness. The conclusion is that this convergence is not coincidental but reflects a deeper structural law (Law I Convergence) governing both acoustic and theological systems.
